strengths: Well-motivated principled Bayesian framework for handling model uncertainty in offline MBRL via BAMDP formulation
Technical contributions including extension of BAMCP to continuous spaces with double progressive widening
Comprehensive experimental evaluation on 12 D4RL tasks and novel tokamak control domain with proper ablations
Multiple algorithm variants enable clear component-wise analysis of contributions
Clear presentation and extensive hyperparameter documentation supporting reproducibility
Practical integration of search into policy iteration framework without requiring test-time search
weaknesses: Inconsistent empirical results: outperforms baselines on only 9/12 D4RL tasks with 3 tasks showing degradation (e.g., med-expert HalfCheetah 90.52 vs 104.2)
Modest average improvement of ~8-10% over SOTA does not justify significantly increased algorithmic complexity
Limited novelty: deep ensembles and reward penalty formulation (Eq. 5) are from prior work (Optimized, MOPO); integration of techniques is relatively straightforward
No convergence guarantees or sample complexity analysis; connection between BAMDP solutions and offline RL performance improvement is not rigorously justified
Critical computational cost analysis missing: no wall-clock time comparisons with baselines; search overhead quantification absent; comparison to MuZero dismissed as unfair

Design choices lack strong justification: arbitrary 10% search frequency lacks ablation, conflation of uncertainty types in reward penalty (Eq. 5) unexplained, belief update IID assumption questionable
Appendix F reveals non-robustness: reward penalty sometimes hurts performance (λ=0 better in some cases), BA-MCTS-SL requires warm-up only on Walker2d suggesting inconsistent behavior
Method introduces many hyperparameters (α, β, c, η, ns, na, ρ, NSL, NP) without sensitivity analysis; inheriting from Optimized may not be optimal
Tokamak evaluation uses synthetic data from learned model, potentially oversimplifying offline RL challenges; limited to 3 tracking tasks
Missing analysis of when/why Bayesian approach helps vs. standard ensembles; no investigation of whether belief actually identifies good models; no characterization of failure modes

strengths: Principled approach to model uncertainty in offline MBRL using Bayes Adaptive framework
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple algorithm variants, ablation studies, and diverse benchmarks (D4RL + tokamak control)
Thorough documentation including extensive hyperparameter tables and design choices in appendices
Addresses practical real-world application (nuclear fusion tokamak control) beyond standard benchmarks
Clear problem motivation and limitations of prior work are well articulated
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (BAMDP, double progressive widening, deep ensembles, reward penalties). No theoretical convergence analysis despite extending BAMCP to continuous spaces

Modest empirical improvements: BA-MCTS achieves ~74.45 vs BA-MBRL ~71.06 on D4RL average, requiring substantial additional computation (MCTS at 10% of states × 50 iterations). No computational cost comparison provided

Unclear technical details: (1) History h representation in feedforward network is never explained; (2) 10% search ratio appears arbitrary with no justification or ablation; (3) Relative contribution of Bayesian belief adaptation vs search component not isolated

Weak justification for core design choices: pessimistic BAMDP via reward penalty is heuristic (directly from Lu et al. 2022); many hyperparameters show task-specific variation (Table 4) without principled selection criteria

Insufficient ablation of core contribution: Appendix F only ablates reward penalty, not belief adaptation itself. BA-MBRL improvement (71.06 vs 65.16 baseline) is modest, suggesting belief adaptation may not be the main driver
History encoding problem: describes π as function of (s,h) with variable-length history h, but implements as feedforward network—a fundamental mismatch never addressed
Mixed experimental results: some tasks show BA-MBRL performing worse than baselines (med-expert HalfCheetah: 90.52 vs 104.2); improvements overlap with error bars in several cases
Unfair baseline comparisons: MuZero adapted for offline via 'reanalyse technique' may not be optimal adaptation; published baseline hyperparameters may not be task-optimal

strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation with principled BAMDP framework for handling model uncertainty in offline MBRL
Solid technical execution: efficient belief updates via ensembles, reasonable extension to continuous spaces using DPW, well-designed policy iteration integration
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with systematic ablations isolating component contributions, two distinct evaluation domains (D4RL + tokamak), multiple seeds with confidence intervals
Clear presentation with detailed algorithms, extensive hyperparameter documentation, and practical reproducibility support
Novel application to challenging tokamak control tasks demonstrating real-world relevance
Valuable practical insight that BA-MCTS-SL is more robust to model inaccuracies than policy gradient methods
weaknesses: Incremental novelty: primarily combines established techniques (BAMDPs, BAMCP, deep ensembles, DPW) rather than introducing fundamentally new concepts
Lack of theoretical analysis: no convergence guarantees for proposed algorithm, break from BAMCP root sampling with DPW only briefly justified, no formal analysis of policy iteration guarantees
Mixed empirical results: outperforms on 9/12 D4RL tasks only; substantial underperformance on some (e.g., HalfCheetah med-expert: 80.53 vs. 104.2); average improvement modest (74.62 vs. 65.16)
Unclear practical benefits of BAMDP over simpler pessimistic MDP approaches; minimal improvement from BA-MBRL to BA-MCTS (only 3.4%) raises questions about Bayesian framework's necessity
Computational cost not thoroughly analyzed: search at 10% of states but overall overhead not reported; high hyperparameter complexity (12+ per-task parameters) with limited sensitivity analysis
Approximation quality of belief update via IID ensemble sampling (Eq. 4) not empirically validated; assumes ensemble members are true posterior samples despite different-initialization training
Hyperparameter sensitivity: Appendix F shows performance sometimes better with λ=0; many alternative design choices in Appendix B without empirical comparison suggest algorithm not fully principled
Limited scope: scalar state/action dimensions (27/14) are modest; scalability to higher-dimensional problems unclear

strengths: Principled application of BAMDPs to offline MBRL with belief adaptation over ensemble members, providing theoretical grounding beyond uniform weighting
Technically sound extension of BAMCP to continuous spaces via double progressive widening, with clear explanation of why root sampling breaks and reasonable PUCT-based solution
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including systematic ablations isolating Bayesian RL vs search components, quantitative belief adaptation analysis, and application to real-world tokamak control
Clear presentation with detailed pseudo-code, comprehensive hyperparameter tables for reproducibility, and promise to release code with standard deviations across multiple seeds
Solid empirical work winning on 9/12 D4RL tasks and showing consistent improvements on the challenging tokamak application
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty as primary contribution is combining established techniques (BAMDPs from Duff 2002, DPW from Auger et al. 2013, deep ensembles from Lakshminarayanan et al. 2017) without major algorithmic innovations

Inconsistent and modest empirical improvements—only wins on 9/12 D4RL tasks, average improvement is ~8% over baseline (74.62 vs 65.16), many results within error bars, and fails on Walker2d without task-specific warm-up phase

Severe hyperparameter sensitivity with task-dependent tuning (Table 4) and no principled selection approach; claim of 'minimal hyperparameter changes' contradicts extensive per-task tuning evident in Tables 3-4

Incomplete analysis of belief adaptation: helps inconsistently across tasks, HalfCheetah-med-expert shows worse performance with adaptive belief (Table 6), and no explanation of when/why it helps despite improvements in prediction metrics

Unjustified design choices: Equation (5) penalty formulation lacks justification; Appendix B defers exploration of multiple design alternatives to future work; belief update treats ensemble as IID samples without sensitivity analysis

Underemphasized computational cost and weak MuZero comparison: Table 11 (training time) relegated to appendix; Sampled EfficientZero performs extremely poorly suggesting unfair adaptation; E-MCTS mentioned but never compared

Significant theory-practice gap: Lemma A.1 justification for root sampling acknowledged as not holding with DPW; no convergence guarantees for proposed Continuous BAMCP with double progressive widening
Limited real-world validation to single tokamak task with learned simulator rather than hardware, overstating real-world applicability claims

strengths: Technically sound algorithmic contributions combining BAMCP with double progressive widening for continuous state/action spaces
Comprehensive experimental methodology with proper ablations isolating individual components (belief adaptation, search, policy update mechanisms)
Extensive reproducibility support including hyperparameter documentation, multiple random seeds, and promised code release
Application to real-world tokamak control demonstrates relevance beyond standard benchmarks
Well-written with clear algorithmic descriptions and proper mathematical formulation
weaknesses: Limited novelty: core components (BAMCP from 2013, DPW, pessimistic MBRL) are well-established; contribution is primarily their combination which is incremental

Empirical gains are modest relative to computational cost: 10-77x training time overhead (Table 11) for 3-10 point D4RL improvement; advantage over recent SOTA (MOBILE) is only 3.75 points when using identical reward penalty (Table 10)

Unjustified technical choices: treating ensemble members as IID Bayesian posterior samples lacks theoretical justification; reward penalty design (Eq. 5) mixes uncertainty types without motivation; DPW workaround for root sampling is unprincipled

Unfair baseline comparisons: Sampled EfficientZero comparison uses an online learning algorithm adapted for offline; main baseline (Optimized) is ~2 years old; Table 10 with recent baselines shows more modest gains
Weak real-world validation: tokamak experiments use learned neural network as simulator, not true physics; reward function provided rather than learned; no evaluation on standard robotics benchmarks
High hyperparameter sensitivity: extensive task-specific tuning (Tables 3-4) with algorithm variants requiring warm-up phases (BA-MCTS-SL on Walker2d), raising overfitting concerns

Unclear component contributions: missing ablation on MCTS without belief adaptation; belief adaptation provides marginal improvements (Table 7, <10% of prediction error in many tasks); BAMDP framework value over simpler uncertainty methods is not demonstrated

Overselling of contributions: comparing to AlphaZero is misleading (different data regime); claims of 'state-of-the-art' are overstated given modest improvements; strong claims about impact not justified by evidence

strengths: Strong and consistent empirical results: Outperforms SOTA offline MBRL methods on 9/12 D4RL tasks with average score of 74.62, and demonstrates superiority on real-world tokamak control tasks
Principled approach to model uncertainty: Modeling offline MBRL as a BAMDP is theoretically motivated and elegantly handles the challenge of multiple MDPs consistent with offline data
Novel technical contribution: Non-trivial extension of BAMCP to continuous state-action spaces with stochastic transitions via integration with double progressive widening

Comprehensive evaluation: Includes ablation studies isolating benefits of BAMDP (RQ1), search (RQ2), and policy updates (RQ3); analysis of belief adaptation effectiveness; comparison with model-free methods; ablation on reward penalty
Thorough belief adaptation analysis: Tables 6-7 and Figure 3 provide good evidence that Bayesian belief updates improve prediction accuracy on most tasks
Excellent reproducibility: Extensive hyperparameter details (Tables 3-4), detailed algorithms, comprehensive appendix with alternative designs, and promised code release
Clear presentation: Algorithm descriptions are clear, motivation is well-articulated, related work is comprehensive, and paper structure is logical
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: Combines well-established techniques (ensembles for uncertainty from MOPO/MOReL/COMBO, double progressive widening from Auger et al. 2013, Bayesian RL with BAMDPs). Contribution is primarily in combination rather than fundamental innovation

Serious concerns about experimental fairness and generalizability: Extensive task-specific hyperparameter tuning (K: 6-13, λ: 0.5-100, H: 5-47, N: 200-1100) raises questions about whether improvements stem from the algorithm or hyperparameter engineering; unclear if approach generalizes without retuning per task
Built on heavily engineered baseline: Implementation based on 'Optimized' (Lu et al., 2022) makes it difficult to isolate improvements from novel components vs. accumulated engineering choices

Critical design choice inadequately justified: Switch from root sampling (BAMCP) to PUCT is relegated to footnote 3 despite affecting core convergence properties; no empirical comparison or analysis of convergence implications; alternative approaches with adaptive beliefs not explored

Substantial computational overhead understated: BA-MCTS requires 2-10x more training time than BA-MBRL (Table 11), yet this cost is characterized as 'limited to training phase' without thorough cost-benefit analysis or deployment timing

Inconsistent belief adaptation benefits: Fails for HalfCheetah-med-expert (Table 6) and hurts performance on 2/12 tasks (Table 7); paper provides no characterization of when/why adaptation helps or hurts; Figure 3 shows single illustrative example

Incomplete technical analysis: No convergence bounds for finite-K belief approximation, no sensitivity analysis for ensemble size K, no sample complexity bounds for Continuous BAMCP, progressive widening parameters held constant without justification

Limited rollout horizons undermine planning benefits: H ranges 5-47 steps to minimize model error, severely limiting tree search depth; no systematic analysis of how H affects performance or whether planning depth justifies computational cost

Supervised learning variant inconsistent: BA-MCTS-SL performs similarly or worse than BA-MCTS (Table 1), requires warm-up phase on Walker2d, suggesting instability; raises questions about its inclusion and utility

Missing ablations and analyses: No empirical comparison of alternative Q̃ formulations (Appendix B), no ensemble size K ablation, no sensitivity analysis for reward penalty formula (Eq. 5), insufficient characterization of hyperparameter sensitivity
Statistical concerns: Some improvements within error bars; no significance testing provided; large standard deviations in some results (e.g., BA-MCTS HalfCheetah med-expert ±10.3)
Unclear scalability: All experiments on relatively modest problems (tokamak is 28D state/14D action); no high-dimensional experiments or analysis of scaling properties

Insufficient MuZero comparison: Sampled EfficientZero performs poorly but explanations are superficial; unclear if poor performance is due to design choices, hyperparameters, or implementation; no tuning attempts for offline setting
Missing comparisons: No comparison with other Bayesian offline RL approaches (Ghosh et al. 2022; Choshen & Tamar, 2023) despite citations
Incomplete guidance: Limited discussion of when approach fails, how to select hyperparameters for new domains, or sensitivity to key design choices
